text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index ended at a record peak on Wednesday as positive signs on the interest rate front and a solid start on Wall Street kept funds flowing into UK shares.
The leading blue chip index rose 20.6 points to 4,281.5, a record close.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade at a record high close, pushed up by firm dollar, supported by Bunds' gains on back of unexpected slide in December manufacturing orders, the DAX index fails to breach the psychologically-key 3,100 point-level after several attempts. The DAX index ended bourse trade up 30.94 points to 3,098.00. In post-bourse the DAX index stood at 3114.73 up 47.25 points.

PARIS - French stocks rallied to a record close on the dollar's strength and expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will not raise U.S. interest rates. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 38.18 points, or 1.53 percent, at 2,541.25, surpassing the previous closing record set last Friday of 2,516.56 points.

ZURICH - Swiss shares for the first time closed above 4,300 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), continuing their latest four-day record run, despite profit taking in the second half of the session. The blue-chip SMI ended 9.0 points higher, or 0.21 percent, at 4,305.5. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) advanced 7.25 points, or 0.26 percent, to 2,750.03.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended the session down, but well off their lows, as they were unable to recover completely from renewed rumours about the financial health of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd which made the bank sector drop with a thud in the morning. The 225-share Nikkei average finished 128.36 points or 0.70 percent lower at 18,185.97.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended higher ahead of the Chinese New Year holiday, buoyed by expectations of a steady, near-term interest rate outlook. The Hang Seng Index jumped 112.07 points or 0.83 percent to close at 13,660.50.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market flew home to a higher finish, lifted by futures-led buying interest and value seeking investors who saw Tuesday's selloff as overdone. At the closer the All Ordinaries index added 26.7 points to 2,435.8.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares swiftly overcame early nervousness to race ahead and post solid gains in heavy trade as positive sentiment continued to sweep through the market. A renewed fall in the bullion price to below $343 -- just a day after a mini-rally sparked hopes of an upturn -- gave dealers a fright early on and most shares opened down. At the closer the All-share index added 38.1 points to 6,804.1 with the Industrials index adds 25.2 points to 8,133.4, Gold shares had a difficult day in the wake of bullion's renewed drop and the index lost 14.6 points to 1,373.7.
